title: The ideal h_A and resolutions of R -> A -> Lambda ⊃ q (Popescu's local problem)
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A$ an $R$-algebra of finite presentation ($A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$), $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras into a commutative ring $\Lambda$, and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal. Put $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt{H_{A/R}\Lambda}\subset\Lambda$, the radical of the ideal of $\Lambda$ generated by $\alpha(H_{A/R})$, where $H_{A/R}$ is the singular ideal of $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. A *resolution* of $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ is a factorization $A\xrightarrow{\beta}B\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda$ of $\alpha$ by homomorphisms of $R$-algebras with $B$ of finite presentation over $R$ such that $\mathfrak h_A\subset\mathfrak h_B$ and $\mathfrak h_B\not\subset\mathfrak q$, where $\mathfrak h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}\Lambda}$ is formed with $\gamma$; $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ *can be resolved* if it has a resolution.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Section 07F6 (section-local): Situation Tag 07F7 (situation-local) and the definition in the paragraph following it ('can be resolved', 'resolution')
